title: A bare playwright run defaulted the generation worker to live mode
body:
## Summary
playwright.config.ts defaulted LLM/AUDIO to replay and PUBLISH to dry but GEN_MODE to live, so any e2e run not started through `pnpm e2e` handed the generation specs' jobs to the real Claude CLI.

## Description
playwright.config.ts:45 (pre-fix) `GEN_MODE: process.env.GEN_MODE ?? "live"` beside `LLM_MODE ?? "replay"`, `AUDIO_MODE ?? "replay"`, `PUBLISH_MODE ?? "dry"` at :37. Only package.json:19 (`pnpm e2e`) set GEN_MODE=fake; e2e/generation.spec.ts:12 and e2e/generation-board.spec.ts:78 skipped only on E2E_LIVE. The worker picks its engine from the mode (apps/server/src/generation/worker-main.ts:46: fake vs createLiveEngine). Fixed: one helper `e2eModes()` in scripts/e2e-preflight.mjs owns every default (replay/replay/dry/fake/no record) for both webServers, and the generation specs skip unless the resolved GEN_MODE is fake.

## Flow
- developer runs `npx playwright test e2e/generation.spec.ts` (or the IDE runner)
- config starts the worker with GEN_MODE=live; spec is not skipped (E2E_LIVE unset)
- POST /api/generation/jobs visual_options -> live engine -> real Claude CLI run
- fix: e2eModes({}) -> GEN_MODE fake; specs skip when the resolved mode is not fake

## Expected impact
Whoever runs one e2e spec by hand: no accidental live generation run (paid model calls, minutes of wall clock). Could break: nothing in `pnpm e2e` (it already set fake); `pnpm e2e:live` now runs its idle worker in fake mode, and its generation specs were already skipped.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every spend-capable e2e mode defaults to its no-spend side
Before: 3 of 4 spend-capable modes defaulted safe (GEN_MODE ?? "live")
After: 4 of 4; e2eModes({}).GEN_MODE === "fake"; `playwright test --list` loads 13 tests
Method: gate - new test in scripts/e2e-preflight.test.mjs, seeded red with the old "live" default (1 failed), green after (10/10)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
playwright.config.ts:45 (pre-fix) GEN_MODE: process.env.GEN_MODE ?? "live"
package.json:19 e2e sets GEN_MODE=fake; package.json:20 e2e:live does not
apps/server/src/generation/worker-main.ts:46 config.mode === "fake" ? fakeEngine() : createLiveEngine(...)
seeded: actual GEN_MODE 'live' vs expected 'fake' -> fail; fixed -> pass 10 fail 0

title: just check passed its scripts, board and opa steps on zero tests
body:
## Summary
`node --test <glob>` and `opa test <dir>` exit 0 when nothing matches, so three of the eight `just check` steps would report PASS after their tests were moved or renamed.

## Description
scripts/check.mjs (pre-fix) ran `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs`, `node --test .claude/skills/board/tests/*.mjs` and `.tools/opa test policy`. Probed: `node --test nothing/*.test.mjs` -> "tests 0", exit 0; `opa test <empty dir>` -> exit 0. Registry quality-gates/gate-liveness: assert the instrument before the result. Fixed: requirePopulation() in scripts/check-core.mjs; check.mjs lists each step's files first (scripts/check.mjs:51-61) and an empty population is FAIL naming the pattern; node --test gets the explicit list.

## Flow
- board tests move to .claude/skills/board/test/ (or scripts tests are renamed *.spec.mjs)
- check runs node --test on a glob matching nothing -> exit 0 -> PASS
- fix: the step lists its files, zero -> FAIL "no files match ..."

## Expected impact
Everyone reading the PASS/FAIL table: a vacuous PASS cannot hide a lost suite. Could break: a step whose dir is legitimately empty now fails loudly (none today).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a check step cannot pass having tested nothing
Before: zero-population node --test and opa test steps -> PASS (exit 0); nodeTestStep with the old glob runner -> ok:true
After: ok:false "no files match scripts/no-such-dir/ ..."; real tree scripts (21 tests) / board (1 file) / opa (106/106) PASS with the same population
Method: gate - new check-core tests, seeded red with today's glob runner (1 failed), green 7/7; `node scripts/check.mjs --only scripts,board,opa` exit 0
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
node --test "nothing/*.test.mjs" -> tests 0, EXIT=0
.tools/opa.exe test <empty> -> EXIT=0
scripts/check.mjs:51-61 nodeTestStep / opaTest
scripts/check-core.mjs requirePopulation

title: The Biome ratchet passed when biome walked zero files
body:
## Summary
A biome walk that matched no file reported an empty diagnostics list, which the ratchet read as every rule decreased - PASS, exit 0 - and the report invited `--update` to bake in zero.

## Description
scripts/biome-ratchet.mjs counted report.diagnostics without checking that any file was walked; Biome's summary carries changed/unchanged file counts (418 on this tree). Registry quality-gates/gate-liveness and excess-indicts-the-instrument (a population implausibly small indicts the instrument). Fixed: instrumentProblem() in scripts/biome-ratchet-core.mjs asserts changed+unchanged > 0 before compare or --update; zero -> exit 2 with the cause.

## Flow
- biome.json files.includes or the ignore file drops apps/packages/e2e
- biome returns {diagnostics: []}; ratchet prints "ratchet ok (0 diagnostics)" and "lock the gain in with --update"
- fix: "biome walked 0 files ..." exit 2

## Expected impact
The director (owner of the baseline): a misconfigured walk can no longer pass, nor be re-baselined to zero. Could break: nothing on a tree with files.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the ratchet cannot report clean on a walk that read nothing
Before: probe --root <git-init'd biome.json + empty apps/packages/e2e> -> "biome ratchet ok (0 diagnostics, none above baseline)", exit 0, 25 rules "decreased"
After: same probe -> "biome walked 0 files ...", exit 2; real tree walks 418 files and reaches the compare
Method: gate - new biome-ratchet test red (missing export) then green 5/5; probe re-run on the real change
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
probe output pre-fix: biome ratchet ok (0 diagnostics, none above baseline) EXIT=0
biome JSON summary: {"changed":0,"unchanged":0,...} with stderr "No files were processed in the specified paths"
post-fix: ZERO-WALK EXIT=2

title: dbt-parse step stayed green on dbt deprecation warnings
body:
## Summary
The dbt-parse step ran `dbt parse` without --warn-error, so deprecations (slated to become errors), empty selectors and orphan config paths printed a warning and the step passed.

## Description
scripts/check.mjs dbtParse (pre-fix) args had no warn-error; the dbt round found 10 MissingArgumentsPropertyInGenericTestDeprecation occurrences that `just check` had passed, fixed those and guarded that one class in pytest. Registry quality-gates/severity-by-construction: a rule that only warns at a gate that ignores warnings enforces nothing. Verified `dbt parse --help` lists --warn-error. Fixed: exported dbtParseArgs() with --warn-error (scripts/check.mjs:20-22).

## Flow
- a model YAML puts a generic-test argument at the top level
- dbt parse warns MissingArguments...Deprecation: 1 occurrence, exit 0 -> PASS
- fix: --warn-error -> exit 2 -> FAIL

## Expected impact
The data lane: the next dbt deprecation is caught at the offline gate, not at the dbt upgrade that turns it into an error. Could break: any future harmless warning now fails the step (real tree: 0 warnings).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - dbt warnings fail the parse gate
Before: seeded copy of pipeline/dbt (1 top-level generic-test arg) -> deprecation printed, exit 0
After: same seeded copy with --warn-error -> exit 2; real tree -> exit 0 (check --only dbt-parse PASS 12.0s)
Method: gate - seeded probe on a temp copy both sides; dbtParseArgs test red (missing export) then green 8/8
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
seeded: [WARNING][MissingArgumentsPropertyInGenericTestDeprecation] ... EXIT=0
seeded --warn-error: EXIT=2
real --warn-error: EXIT=0

title: playwright.config.ts and vitest.config.ts were outside the typecheck graph
body:
## Summary
`pnpm typecheck` (tsc -b on tsconfig.json) included apps, packages and e2e but not the two root configs, so the file wiring every e2e webServer and mode env was never type-checked.

## Description
tsconfig.json include (pre-fix) ["apps/*/src", "packages/*/src", "e2e"]; `tsc --listFilesOnly` listed 0 of the 2 configs, and scripts/e2e-preflight.d.mts exists only to type playwright.config.ts's import. Registry test-harness/out-of-graph-artifacts. Fixed: both configs added to include.

## Flow
- edit playwright.config.ts with a type error (wrong env shape, renamed helper)
- pnpm typecheck exit 0; the break surfaces only when e2e runs (director-only, minutes)
- fix: tsc reports it

## Expected impact
Anyone editing e2e wiring: a type error fails the cheap gate instead of the 25-minute e2e. Could break: nothing (both configs type-check clean).

## Evaluation

Before: seeded `const seededTypeError: number = "not a number"` in playwright.config.ts -> pnpm -s typecheck exit 0
After: same seed -> TS2322 playwright.config.ts(53,7), exit 1; seed removed -> exit 0
Method: gate - seeded type error both sides
Result: better

title: just setup put .tools under a percent-encoded path for a spaced repo path
body:
## Summary
scripts/setup-tools.mjs derived the repo root from URL.pathname, which keeps %20 and %C3%AB, so a checkout under a path with a space or non-ASCII letter got its OPA in a literal "John%20Doe" tree.

## Description
scripts/setup-tools.mjs:9 (pre-fix) `new URL(import.meta.url).pathname.replace(/^\/(\w:)/, "$1")`; every other script (scripts/check.mjs:11, scripts/biome-ratchet.mjs:13, scripts/e2e-preflight.mjs:13, scripts/font-metrics.mjs:18) uses fileURLToPath, and check.mjs looks for .tools/opa under the real root, so opa would fail ENOENT right after setup printed "tools ready". Fixed: fileURLToPath.

## Flow
- owner clones into C:/Users/John Doe/StatReel and runs just setup
- OPA downloaded to C:/Users/John%20Doe/StatReel/.tools
- just check -> opa step ENOENT
- fix: root resolves to the real path

## Expected impact
A fresh machine with a spaced or accented profile path: setup works first time. Could break: nothing (identical result on plain paths).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - setup-tools resolves the real repo root
Before: probe over 3 paths -> 2 of 3 roots wrong (John%20Doe, Zo%C3%AB)
After: 3 of 3 equal to the expected root
Method: probe - the root derivation run on both sides over 3 paths (running setup itself downloads, so not run)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: secrets-set crashed when run from anywhere but the repo root
body:
## Summary
scripts/secrets-set.mjs resolved the keyring package through the cwd, so running it from a subdirectory died with "Cannot find module '@napi-rs/keyring'".

## Description
scripts/secrets-set.mjs:11 (pre-fix) `createRequire(path.resolve("apps/server/package.json"))` - cwd-relative, unlike every sibling script. `just secrets-set` was safe (just runs in the justfile dir); `node scripts/secrets-set.mjs` from elsewhere was not. This is the round's invocation-location class. Fixed: anchored to the script's own path.

## Flow
- cd apps && node ../scripts/secrets-set.mjs elevenlabs
- Error: Cannot find module '@napi-rs/keyring' before the prompt
- fix: module resolves; prompt appears

## Expected impact

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the script works from any cwd
Before: from apps/: Error: Cannot find module '@napi-rs/keyring'
After: from apps/ and root: "empty value, nothing stored" (empty probe stdin; nothing reached the keychain)
Method: probe - same command both sides with an empty value
Result: better

title: just test-all advertised everything offline and ran 3 of 8 gates
body:
## Summary
`just test-all` ("everything that runs offline") ran vitest, opa and pytest only and stopped at the first red line, beside the `just check` gate built to replace it; check's own comment named 6 of its 8 steps.

## Description
justfile:47-51 (pre-fix) test-all recipe; justfile:53 check comment omitted the board harness and Biome ratchet. Registry quality-gates/policy-projection: surfaces understate what blocks. Fixed: `alias test-all := check`; comment lists all 8 steps.

## Flow
- contributor reads `just --list`, runs `just test-all` as the offline gate
- typecheck, script tests, board, dbt parse, ratchet never run; first failure hides the rest
- fix: test-all is check

## Expected impact
Anyone choosing a gate from `just --list`. Could break: muscle memory expecting the 3-step version (alias keeps the name).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the advertised offline gate runs every offline step
Before: test-all 3/8 gates, abort-on-first-failure; check comment 6/8 steps
After: `just test-all --only opa` -> check's table, ALL PASS; `just --list` names 8/8 and shows [alias: test-all]
Method: probe - recipe run both sides; step count from scripts/check.mjs STEPS
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
justfile (pre-fix) test-all: pnpm test / .tools/opa test policy / uv pytest
scripts/check.mjs STEPS: typecheck, vitest, scripts, board, pytest, opa, dbt-parse, biome-ratchet

title: pnpm format rewrote the whole tree with Biome against the repo law
body:
## Summary
The root package.json shipped `"format": "biome format --write ."`, a one-keystroke repo-wide Biome write that the repo law and owner memory forbid.

## Description
package.json:16 (pre-fix). .claude/perfect/config.md repo law: never run biome format --write over directories (HEAD is not Biome-clean; the debt is held by scripts/biome-ratchet.mjs). Registry quality-gates/prose-rule-drift. Fixed: script removed; scripts/biome-ratchet.test.mjs fails if any root script pairs biome with --write.

## Flow
- contributor runs `pnpm format` expecting a harmless tidy
- every file in apps/packages/e2e is rewritten, including other sessions' in-flight work
- fix: no such script; a test keeps it out

## Expected impact
Concurrent sessions and the owner's review diff. Could break: anyone who used `pnpm format` (grep: 0 references) formats per file instead.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no workspace script violates the Biome write rule
Before: 1 root script with a repo-wide Biome --write; new test red (offender: format)
After: 0; test green 6/6
Method: gate - new scripts test red then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

package.json:16 "format": "biome format --write ."

title: just heatmap ignored STATREEL_PORT and died with an undici stack
body:
## Summary
The heatmap recipe POSTed to a hard-coded 127.0.0.1:8787 and printed an unhandled undici stack when nothing listened; a non-2xx crashed on j.cells.

## Description
justfile:33 (pre-fix). The server listens on STATREEL_PORT (apps/server/src/config.ts:88), so a server elsewhere was never reached and whatever owned 8787 was recomputed instead. Registry quality-gates/refusal-names-a-reachable-remedy. Fixed: reads STATREEL_PORT, non-2xx is a failure, one named line with the remedy.

## Flow
- server on STATREEL_PORT=8797; `just heatmap` recomputes whatever is on 8787
- no server: undici stack trace
- fix: named line naming the port and the remedy

## Expected impact
The owner after a transform. Could break: nothing (default port unchanged).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the recipe reaches the configured server and fails legibly
Before: dry-run with STATREEL_PORT=59999 -> URL :8787; no server -> undici stack, exit 1
After: "heatmap: no recompute from 127.0.0.1:59999 (ECONNREFUSED) - start the server with pnpm dev, or set STATREEL_PORT ...", exit 1
Method: probe - recipe run through the justfile's PowerShell shell on an unused port (not against the live dev server, which would recompute its DB)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
pre: node:internal/deps/undici/undici:15845 Error.captureStackTrace(err)
post: heatmap: no recompute from 127.0.0.1:59999 (ECONNREFUSED) ...

title: Biome ratchet format count measures working-tree CRLF, not committed content
body:
## Summary
The ratchet runs biome over the working tree, where 64 files sit with CRLF despite `* text=auto eol=lf`; the format count differs from the committed content by ~20, so the gate's verdict depends on the checkout, not the change.

## Description
scripts/biome-ratchet.mjs:21-24 checks apps/packages/e2e on disk. `git ls-files --eol` -> 64 w/crlf + 7 w/mixed (i/lf in the index); 63 of those carry a format diagnostic. A `git archive HEAD` export of the same paths measures format 209 against 229-230 on this checkout (baseline 230). On a fresh LF clone the ratchet therefore has ~21 format diagnostics of silent headroom; on a Windows checkout an agent writing CRLF raises the count with no content change. Registry quality-gates/blocking-by-input-determinism and match-the-resolved-artifact (gate sees working tree vs commit content). Fix shape: measure an LF-normalised snapshot (copy ls-files -co --exclude-standard into a temp root, CRLF->LF as git would commit, run with --root), then the director re-baselines.

## Flow
- fresh clone (LF) -> format 209 vs baseline 230 -> 21 new format violations pass silently
- this checkout -> files re-saved with CRLF move the count without a content change
- fix: ratchet measures what would be committed

## Expected impact
The director and every contributor reading the ratchet: one verdict per content. Could break: the baseline must be re-taken (director-only) once the instrument changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the ratchet's verdict is a function of committed content
Before: working tree format 229-230 vs HEAD export 209 for the same paths (20-21 apart)
After: not measured - instrument (normalised snapshot) not built this round
Method: experiment - same ratchet run over the working tree and over a git archive HEAD export; the fix needs a baseline re-take, which is director-only
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
git ls-files --eol apps packages e2e: 64 w/crlf, 7 w/mixed, 358 w/lf
format diagnostics by eol: w/lf 159, w/crlf 63, w/mixed 7
--root <git archive HEAD export> -> format 230 -> 209
instrument: ratchet run on this checkout vs a git-archive HEAD export: per-rule counts must be equal after the change (today format 229 vs 209); seed a CRLF-only re-save of one clean file and watch the count stay flat

title: Biome never reads scripts/ or the root configs - the gate code itself
body:
## Summary
biome.json files.includes covers apps/packages/e2e only, so scripts/*.mjs (check.mjs, the ratchet, the preflight) and playwright/vitest configs are never linted or format-checked.

## Description

A temp config including scripts/** and *.config.ts walks 15 files and finds 12 format diagnostics, 0 lint. Registry test-harness/gate-scope-is-not-report-scope. - a lint-class bug lands in scripts/check.mjs (e.g. an unused variable, a shadowed name)
- no Biome surface sees it; the ratchet reports ok
- fix: scripts are in scope; baseline absorbs the 12 existing format findings

The gate code gets the same lint as the code it gates. Could break: baseline update needed (director-only), so not Lane A.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the linter covers the gate scripts
Before: 0 of 15 tooling files in Biome's walk
After: 15 of 15 (12 format diagnostics to baseline), not applied
Method: probe - biome over the files with a temp config; landing it needs a baseline re-take
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
temp config includes ['**/scripts/**','**/*.config.ts'] -> 15 files 12 diagnostics { format: 12 }
biome.json:3 files.includes
instrument: biome walk count over scripts/ + root configs (0 -> 15) and a seeded lint violation in scripts/ going red in the ratchet; baseline re-taken by the director

title: Replay e2e writes into the owner's real data/generation, board and renders
body:
## Summary
The e2e app DB is fresh per run, but generation jobs, board stills and renders land in the developer's real data/ dirs and are never pruned: 23 e2e job dirs (44 MB) sit in data/generation, and e2e-probe.png / e2e-gen-real.png in data/board/items.

## Description
e2e/generation.spec.ts:43, e2e/generation-board.spec.ts:116,177-178,197 and e2e/m1.spec.ts:139-141 resolve data/... in the real tree; the server writes paths.board / paths.renders under repoRoot/data (apps/server/src/config.ts:16-18); global-setup prunes only data/e2e run DBs (e2e/global-setup.ts:13). All 23 data/generation dirs have e2e case titles (11 "e2e generation probe", 6 "e2e video probe", 6 "e2e visuals probe"). STATREEL_GEN_DATA already exists (apps/server/src/generation/config.ts:60) but paths.board/renders are not overridable. Registry test-harness/isolation-lanes. Spec paths are also cwd-relative (playwright.config.ts:8, e2e/global-setup.ts:11) while the server anchors to repoRoot.

## Flow
- pnpm e2e runs 3 generation jobs and 1 render per run
- outputs land in data/generation, data/board, data/renders with no DB row once the run DB is pruned
- fix: one e2e data root (STATREEL_GEN_DATA + a server data-root override) set by playwright.config for server and worker, specs read it

## Expected impact
The owner's data dirs stop accumulating orphan e2e artefacts; e2e stops depending on dev state. Could break: the server data-root override is server-context code (out of scope here).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - e2e outputs live in an e2e-owned root
Before: 23 of 23 data/generation dirs are e2e leftovers (44 MB); 2 e2e PNGs in data/board/items
After: not measured - needs a server-side data-root override
Method: simulation - counted the leftovers on this tree; the fix crosses into apps/server (out-of-scope)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
for d in data/generation/*: case.json title -> 11 e2e generation probe, 6 e2e video probe, 6 e2e visuals probe
ls data/board/items | grep e2e -> e2e-gen-real.png, e2e-probe.png
apps/server/src/config.ts:16-18 renders/board under repoRoot/data
instrument: after one replay run, count e2e-titled dirs under data/generation and e2e files under data/board (today +3 dirs/run) -> 0 in the real data dir

title: The live-marker text names `just e2e-live` and `pnpm e2e:live`; neither runs it

- runs `just e2e-live` -> just: recipe not found; runs `pnpm e2e:live` -> Playwright, paid audio, no pytest
- fix: the text names the real recipe

## Expected impact
Whoever wants the live ingest test. Could break: nothing (text).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the named remedy resolves
Before: 0 of 2 named commands run the live test
After: 1 of 1 (just e2e-pipeline-live), not applied
Method: probe - `just --list` has no e2e-live; package.json e2e:live runs playwright
Result: better
Gate: none

pipeline/pyproject.toml:31 markers = ["live: ... (pnpm e2e:live / just e2e-live)"]

title: Five documented policy gates call `opa`, which is not on PATH
body:
## Summary
The manifest capability, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md and both sweep overlays give the policy gate as `opa test policy`, but OPA is installed only as .tools/opa(.exe) by just setup - the documented command fails "not found" on this machine.

## Description
.ai/manifest.yaml:17 policy-test, CLAUDE.md:22, DESIGN.md:512, .claude/scan-sweep/config.md:22, .claude/perfect/config.md:32. `which opa` -> none; justfile:37 and scripts/check.mjs use .tools/opa. This is the round's "gate whose selection depends on where it is invoked" class: the command works only on a machine that also put OPA on PATH. Fix: name `just policy-test` or `pnpm check --only opa`. All five files are outside this context (owner docs / director overlays).

## Flow
- agent reads the manifest capability, runs `opa test policy`
- "opa: command not found" -> the gate is reported as unrunnable or skipped
- fix: docs name the repo's own entry point

## Expected impact
Every agent and the owner choosing the policy gate from the docs. Could break: nothing (text).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - documented gate commands run from a fresh setup
Before: 5 doc sites name a bare `opa`; `which opa` -> not found
After: 0, not applied (out of scope)
Method: probe - PATH lookup on this machine; grep of the five sites
Result: better

title: just setup downloads OPA "latest" unpinned and unverified
body:
## Summary
scripts/setup-tools.mjs fetches openpolicyagent.org/downloads/latest/<asset> with no version pin and no checksum, so the opa gate's engine differs by the day setup ran, and an executable is installed unverified.

## Description
scripts/setup-tools.mjs:27 `downloads/latest/${asset}`; the x64 Node zip is version-pinned (v22.23.3) but also unverified (scripts/setup-tools.mjs:32). This machine runs OPA 1.21.1 from .tools. Registry quality-gates/blocking-by-input-determinism (a verdict must be a function of the tree) and supply-chain. Fix shape: pin the OPA version this tree is green on (1.21.1) and verify the published sha256 for both downloads. Needs network to fetch and confirm the checksums, so not built in a no-network round.

## Flow
- two machines run just setup months apart
- they gate policy/ with different OPA engines; a rego change green on one is red on the other
- fix: pinned version + checksum

## Expected impact
Reproducible policy gate across machines; tampered download refused. Could break: an OPA bump becomes an explicit edit.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the policy engine is pinned and verified
Before: 0 of 2 downloads checksum-verified; OPA version floats (latest)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - read the download path; verifying a checksum needs the network
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: setup on a scratch .tools: URL contains the pinned version and a tampered byte in the downloaded file fails the sha256 check

title: secrets-set echoes the pasted key to the terminal
body:
## Summary
secrets-set reads the key from stdin in cooked mode, so the terminal echoes it in full while the prompt says "input is not echoed to logs".

## Description
scripts/secrets-set.mjs:17-18 (`process.stdin` without setRawMode); the prompt copy at scripts/secrets-set.mjs:15. A pasted ElevenLabs key stays in terminal scrollback and any screen share. Fix shape: when stdin is a TTY, setRawMode(true) and read until Enter without echo (fall back to piped stdin unchanged).

## Flow
- owner runs just secrets-set elevenlabs and pastes the key
- the key is printed on screen and kept in scrollback
- fix: no echo on a TTY

## Expected impact
The owner's API key stays off screen. Could break: paste handling in raw mode on some terminals.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the secret is not displayed
Before: key echoed on a TTY (cooked mode)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - no TTY in this session to drive the prompt
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: scripts/secrets-set.mjs: process.stdin.setEncoding('utf8'); for await (const chunk of process.stdin) ... (no setRawMode)
instrument: a pty-driven run (node-pty or `script`): the captured terminal output after the prompt contains no byte of the typed value
